title: Georgia
subtitle: from Tbilisi to the Black Sea
standfirst: Photos from Georgia in August 2015: Tbilisi, Gori, then west to Batumi on the Black Sea, before crossing into Turkey for Trabzon.

cover.alt: Brick houses with iron balconies in Tbilisi, lit by late sun

stops.caption: Tbilisi, on the Mtkvari river. Brick houses with iron balconies on the streets, wooden galleries round the courtyards behind them.

photos.alt: A row of brick houses with wrought-iron balconies and a satellite dish, trees to the right
A workshop doorway in a peeling wall, a hand-painted list of repairs in red Georgian script beside it
A vaulted stone arcade, blank canvases and paints laid out on the steps
A painter at an easel between stone columns, paintings for sale propped along the steps
Crates of black grapes and plums, lined with Georgian newspaper
Weathered wooden galleries and brick walls around a Tbilisi courtyard

stops.caption: Gori, on the plain of Shida Kartli. Stalin was born here; the house he grew up in and his railway carriage stand in the museum grounds.

photos.alt: The wooden door and window of Stalin's childhood house, a Russian plaque naming it a house-museum
The green side of a Soviet railway carriage, the USSR emblem between curtained windows
A road sign in Georgian and English pointing left to Gori and right to Sveneti, poplars behind

stops.caption: Batumi, on the Black Sea a few kilometres from the Turkish border. Low pastel streets in the old town, Soviet blocks behind, a pebble beach in front.

photos.alt: A pebble beach with umbrellas and sun loungers along a flat blue Black Sea
A cobbled old-town street of pink houses leading to the Alphabetic Tower
Three Soviet apartment blocks with blue and green balconies under a mackerel sky
